tickets.title: Write the agent guide this repo has never had
tickets.detail:
There is no CLAUDE.md, no AGENTS.md, no .cursorrules. Every trap an agent needs is real but scattered: MEMORY_LANE.md (history, sections 4/5/6), README.md (concepts and the settings tables), RELEASING.md (branches), and the board's own context packs.
A guide here should be short and should NOT restate the README. What it must carry: the module split (core = runtime, editor = the tool, demo = the example), the rule that Kryo registration order is a file format (GVars_Serialization), that core is release=11 while everything else is 17, that the editor's state is static GVars_* with one project at a time, that compiling proves nothing in the editor package (run it), and the gates — ./gradlew build, ./gradlew :core:test, ./gradlew :editor:run, ./gradlew :demo:run.
Same standard as the context packs: name files and commands, never advice. If a line would be true in any repo, cut it.
Note (fedora1-parallax-4): Retagged from #docs (dropped by d2/B) to #runtime #format #editor #build. Each thing this guide must carry comes out of one of those packs: module split, release=11 vs 17 and the Gradle gates (build); Kryo registration order (format); static GVars_* and 'compiling proves nothing, run it' (editor); core = runtime, :core:test and :demo:run (runtime). The guide condenses those packs, so whoever writes it needs all four loaded — that is the gate, deliberately. #assets and #project-io are left off because r3 asks for nothing from them; add them if the guide grows to cover flatten/

tickets.title: driver-probe.sh's BindException check runs before its own editor can have logged one

WRONG: tools/driver-probe.sh (r43, ef0586a) checks the port before launching, then waits in a loop that breaks as soon as port_open succeeds, then greps editor/build/driver-probe.log for BindException. In the race r43 meant to catch (another editor takes the port between the check and our bind), port_open succeeds at once because the OTHER editor answers, so the grep runs a second or less after launch, before our JVM has started and logged the BindException. The script then drives the other editor, which is what r40 did.

Also by reading: saving elsewhere breaks RELATIVE loose-image paths the same way (resolved against the new folder on reopen). Note .plaxpj is the editor's Jackson JSON, not the Kryo .plax format, and preload already accepts a path in atlasName ('../Demos/OneNight.atlas' would load) - so a relative/absolute atlas path in the PROJECT file needs no .plax format bump, as long as the export keeps the bare nam

tickets.title: Start screen file chooser: Up/Down/Backspace/Left keys do nothing
tickets.detail:
Found by the r5 sweep. editor/src/jks/tools2d/filechooser/FC_List.java keyControlsListener handles DEL (back), LEFT (up) and UP/DOWN (move the selection) inside keyTyped() through event.getKeyCode(). Stage.keyTyped only sets the character, never a key code, so those branches never run: in the sweep, DOWN/UP left the selection unchanged, and DEL/LEFT left the folder unchanged. Only Enter works, because it is tested on the character. Fix: handle those keys in keyDown(), then run the editor and use them.
Note (fedora1-parallax-6): keyDown handler written (skips when the event is handled or the path field has focus, so the List's own UP/DOWN and typing in the path are untouched). Also focusing the chooser in Vue_Selection.init: before, nothing held focus on the start screen so no key reached it until a row was clicked. Next: drive it in the /tmp/r5h harness.

Commit a0c6f69 (develop, unpushed). FC_List: DEL/LEFT/UP/DOWN moved from keyTyped to keyDown (Enter stays in keyTyped, it is a character). keyDown skips when the path field has focus (else backspace in the path would go Back) and when the event is already handled (the libGDX List moves its own selection on UP/DOWN when it holds focus, which would otherwise move 2 rows). Also Vue_Selection.init now focuses the chooser: before, nothing held focus on the start screen, so for a real user no key worked until a row was clicked (the r5 sweep forced the focus by hand).
